content.text:
**Finding submitted: deviation (§ 19.2).**

The warranty article is largely sound — § 19.1 (professional and workmanlike + conformance), § 19.3 (Applicable Law, malicious code, no functionality diminishment, OSS protection), § 19.4 (re-perform/repair/replace with refund fallback, non-exclusive for key claims), and § 19.5 (disclaimer expressly does not limit express warranties) all meet or exceed the preferred position.

The single material failure is duration: § 19.2 caps the Deliverable conformance warranty at fifteen days and then extinguishes Vendor's correction and refund obligations altogether, which overrides the unqualified § 19.1 conformance warranty and hollows out the § 19.4 remedy. Fifteen days sits below the fallback floor (90 days software / 30 days services) and, against the fifteen *business* day acceptance window in § 6.1, the warranty would lapse before acceptance testing even closes.

Redline (validated, ok:true): extend to ninety (90) days and delete the cut-off sentence, cross-referencing the existing § 19.4 remedy rather than adding new remedy language.
